title: Tickets Giveaway
transcript: Gotham Chess falls to his knees on stage and Judit Polgar celebrates after the move that I played in this position. You see, this is a game that took place in Stockholm during an event called Chess Party. Levy Rozman, Judit Polgar, myself, and Sabri Cano and I were playing what is called Hand and Brain, a chess variant where you are in pairs and one player names a piece and the other player has to decide a move with that piece. Judit and Sabri had the white pieces and Levy and I were playing with the black pieces and we entered this weird sideline of the Sicilian with b3 and g6 and despite the weird nature of the game, we played a pretty solid game and the game was balanced for most of the time. And for the record, Sabri is about 2400 online, so I was definitely a little bit on the spot here. We trade queens, we continue the game, I offer a rook trade, and eventually we reach this position right here. Judit told Sabri to move a pawn and she probably meant b4, preventing a bishop check with bishop to c5, but Sabri blunders and actually takes on c4. And in this moment, Levy tells me, "Bishop, bishop." Trying to get me to find the move bishop to c5, but at this point I have 27 seconds on the clock and I do not see this move. And since I don't see that move for some reason, I play bishop to g2 and this is that exact moment. >> Thank you. >> Did I mess up? >> Yeah, I did. >> Oh, no. No. >> And by the way, if you want to attend an event like this in person in London on the 10th of November this year, all you have to do is follow me and leave a comment under this video and I will randomly extract two lucky winners that will get a ticket to go to the Gotham Chess tour and I will be there myself. Unfortunately, from here, the game went on and eventually both myself and Sabri took over the game and started playing on our own. And eventually Sabri was able to win this game by checkmating me like this.
